editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format), 556 words within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral, factual tone throughout with no editorializing or AI self-reference. No sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 cited sources personally read and checked against every claim they support. sources-0/1/3/4.html.gz snapshots decompressed and their sha256 hashes verified against manifest.json (all match). source-2 (power-technology.com) snapshot failed with HTTP 403 (bot-blocked); per protocol I fell back to a live WebFetch of https://www.power-technology.com/news/ocean-winds-consent-2gw-caledonia-offshore-project/ and confirmed its content matches the claims and quotes attributed to it (the Mark Baxter and Adam Morrison quotes, the 200-skilled-positions workforce figure, the ScotWind/Aberdeenshire Council references, and the 2030/CfD/FID construction timeline all appear verbatim/consistent in the live page). Findings: (1) gov.scot [source-0.html.gz] — confirms headline, summary, 429km2 area, 140-turbine cap, £1.7bn supply-chain commitment, 2-million-household figure, the John Swinney quote (verbatim), the Caledonia South foundation-mix quote (verbatim), and the seabird compensation plan requirement, all verbatim/consistent. (2) offshorewind.biz [source-1.html.gz] — confirms 2GW/429km2/140-turbine topline, the 40-100m water depth range, onshore consent by Aberdeenshire Council, ScotWind leasing round, and 2030 construction subject to CfD/FID — but does NOT contain the 77-turbine (Caledonia North) / 78-turbine (Caledonia South) / 39-floating-turbine breakdown that the article attributes to it (see Findings below; that breakdown is sourced from gov.scot instead). (3) power-technology.com [WebFetch fallback, snapshot 403] — confirms both direct quotes attributed to it (Baxter 'culmination of years of hard work...', Morrison 'built on Ocean Winds' proud legacy...write the next chapter'), the 200-skilled-positions figure, ScotWind and Aberdeenshire Council references, and 2030/CfD/FID timeline. (4) agcc.co.uk [source-3.html.gz] — confirms both Baxter quotes verbatim, the 200-skilled-positions figure, and the ScotWind/onshore-consent context; note this page is captioned 'by Ocean Winds UK' and 'Member News', i.e. a republished company press release rather than independent reporting. (5) energyglobal.com [source-4.html.gz] — confirms both Baxter quotes and the Morrison quote verbatim; text is near-identical to the AGCC press release, indicating sources 3 and 4 substantially reproduce the same underlying Ocean Winds press release rather than being fully independent reporting (noted as a source-diversity observation, not an accuracy problem — the facts are independently corroborated by gov.scot and offshorewind.biz).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One recoverable misattribution found: the bullet 'Ocean Winds is splitting the capacity evenly between the two sites, with up to 140 turbines total — 77 for Caledonia North and 78 for Caledonia South, including as many as 39 floating turbines — across water depths of 40 to 100 meters, according to Offshore Wind' cites the entire sentence to offshorewind.biz, but the 77/78/39 turbine breakdown does not appear anywhere in the offshorewind.biz snapshot (verified by keyword search — '77', '78', '39', and 'floating turbine' are all absent from the extracted text). That specific breakdown instead comes verbatim from the gov.scot snapshot ('up to 77 offshore Wind Turbine Generators' for Caledonia North; 'up to 78 Wind Turbine Generators (of which no more than 39 shall be floating)' for Caledonia South). Only the 40-100m water-depth figure in that bullet is actually supported by offshorewind.biz. The underlying numbers are all true and independently verifiable in the article's own gov.scot citation elsewhere in the piece — this is a citation/attribution error, not a fabrication — so it is filed as a corrections record rather than grounds for rejection. All other specifics, quotes, and figures in the article trace correctly to their cited sources with no hallucinations detected.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Attributions are consistent, quotes are clearly marked, and the 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags open items (CfD, FID, seabird compensation plan) rather than presenting the project as a fait accompli.

concerns: The 'Ocean Winds is splitting the capacity evenly...' bullet misattributes the 77/78-turbine and 39-floating-turbine breakdown to Offshore Wind (offshorewind.biz) when that specific breakdown is sourced from gov.scot; only the 40-100m water depth figure in that sentence is actually supported by the Offshore Wind snapshot.
